title: Imhotep
summary: Imhotep was an official of the Egyptian king Djoser, credited as the architect of Djoser's Step Pyramid at Saqqara; an inscription bearing his name was found on a statue of Djoser at the site. Later tradition made him a physician and author, and he was worshipped as a deity in later periods, but his medical role and writings are debated.

uncertainty.note: Sources give fl. 2667 BCE - 2600 BCE and c. 2667-2600 BCE. Dates are approximate; neither source says how they were derived.

where.modern_name: Saqqara, Giza Governorate, Egypt (pinned to the site of Djoser's Step Pyramid, the work most associated with him; his birthplace and burial are not given in the sources)
where.historical_name: Saqqara, necropolis of Memphis, Egypt under King Djoser (Third Dynasty)

importance.justification: Credited as architect of the Step Pyramid and, in later tradition, associated with medicine and deified.

reviewer_note: His existence is supported by the inscription on the Djoser statue; the medical and literary attributions (e.g. Edwin Smith Papyrus c. 1600 BCE) and deification are later tradition. Museum publisher name taken from the domain; operating institution not confirmed. Pin is the Saqqara village centroid.
